baseline_note: Primary-source mechanism review and original teaching diagrams only. Chinese segmentation, vocabulary IDs, vector values and the two senses of apple are illustrative; no actual tokenizer, trained embedding, contextual model output or model training was executed. The diagrams omit special tokens, positional mechanisms and other model inputs. Pinned Hugging Face and PyTorch files are independent reading baselines, not a tested dependency combination. Dynamic page last_updated is the displayed date and no page mirror is stored. The arbitrary lookup examples do not establish semantic similarity or trained model capability.

claims.statement: Tokenization, vocabulary IDs and input embedding lookup form separate stages. The Chinese segmentation, ID mapping and three-dimensional vectors are original teaching examples.

claims.section: 2 Token 和 ID 各自的作用
claims.statement: Token boundaries depend on the tokenizer and the vocabulary must match the model. ID proximity has no inherent semantic meaning; this explanation follows the indexing mechanism.
Embedding retrieves fixed-length vectors by integer index from a parameter table; interpreting each dimension as a named human property is not generally justified.
Embedding weights can be initialized and trained or loaded and optionally frozen; learning the table is distinct from changing a fixed tokenizer vocabulary.

Causal language modeling constructs prediction targets from text. Forward computation, loss evaluation, backward gradient computation and optimizer update have separate roles; token IDs are categorical targets, not a numerical-distance regression objective.
Ordinary inference evaluates current parameters without an optimizer training update.

claims.section: 5 从初始向量到上下文表示
claims.statement: The same token lookup under unchanged parameters returns the same initial vector; subsequent network computation can incorporate visible context. Causal prediction excludes unseen future tokens.
